description: Proyecto que analiza datos de observación de la NASA para detectar cambios y tendencias en el sistema terrestre. Reunimos series de tiempo satelitales, las organizamos en una base de datos eficiente y las convertimos en visualizaciones interactivas que muestran cómo evolucionan variables como temperatura, vegetación o cobertura de hielo a lo largo de los años.
summary: We built a tool that analyzes NASA GISTEMP temperature records by latitude zone since 1880 to answer the challenge questions: what is changing, where, how much, and whether the change is significant. For each of the 14 zones we compute a linear trend and its p-value, and we visualize the results. All zones show significant warming, but not equally: the Arctic (64N-90N) warms about 0.19 °C per decade, roughly 2.3 times the global average (0.083 °C per decade), while the mid-southern latitudes warm the least. This helps identify which regions are changing fastest.
details: Using Python (pandas, SciPy, matplotlib) we load the NASA GISTEMP zonal annual temperature anomalies, compute a linear regression per latitude zone, and report the trend in °C per decade with its p-value. Two visualizations show the trend by zone and the temporal evolution of the Arctic, global and Antarctic series. Result: all 14 zones show significant warming (p < 0.05), with the Arctic warming fastest. Limitation: simple linear regression does not account for autocorrelation in the time series, so p-values may be overstated. Next steps: add more variables (vegetation, ice cover) and a database layer for interactive exploration. The code was developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic), an SI tool.
